description: Prepares owner review for a new BotSpot deployment; this call does not start a bot or place trades before approval. After explicit owner approval, this is HIGH RISK: the deployment may place real-money trades. Call for an authorized start request even when required saved variables are missing: readiness validation returns the exact missing-variable secure entry cards. Preparing those cards is the next setup step, not a completed start or approval. Never request secret values in chat or claim a schedule was created by this preparation. For an extra iteration of an existing scheduled bot, use run_deployment_once; do not create another deployment. Never use this tool for a direct or one-off buy, sell, or order request. Use place_trade instead; a start_deployment approval is not a trade approval. When the user asks to run, start, turn on, or deploy an attached saved strategy, call this tool to create the website approval request; do not substitute a backtest. Omit brokerCredentialId by default unless the user explicitly named the exact saved broker connection/account to use now. The website approval page is the normal place for visible broker selection and blocks approval until a valid broker is selected. This tool accepts only saved references: aiStrategyRevisionId for code, optional brokerCredentialId for broker access, and optional envVarSetIds for saved non-broker runtime secrets. Broker access must come from a saved broker credential selected in the tool call or on the website approval page. Do not pass a broker credential whose status is reconnect_required. Omit brokerCredentialId and still create the start approval; the website approval page lets the owner select, add, or reconnect a broker before approving, including through /account-settings/broker-connections. Non-broker runtime secrets must come from saved environment variables: pass their ids as envVarSetIds. Do not pass raw broker credentials, raw environment variables, raw runtime configuration, inline code, requirements text, API keys, screener exports, CSV rows, JSON row dumps, workbook data, or large base64 blobs. Use create_broker_credential/list_broker_credentials before deployment, and use saved_env_vars(action="create")/saved_env_vars(action="list") for data-provider API keys or other non-broker runtime secrets. Broker credential key examples: Alpaca (alpaca): ALPACA_API_KEY + ALPACA_API_SECRET OR ALPACA_OAUTH_TOKEN. Do not pass ALPACA_IS_PAPER; BotSpot derives it from paperOrLive. Example credentialValues: {"ALPACA_API_KEY":"PK...","ALPACA_API_SECRET":"secret..."}. Tradier (tradier): TRADIER_ACCOUNT_NUMBER + TRADIER_ACCESS_TOKEN OR TRADIER_ACCOUNT_NUMBER + TRADIER_API_KEY OR TRADIER_ACCOUNT_NUMBER + TRADIER_TOKEN. Optional: TRADIER_REFRESH_TOKEN, TRADIER_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, TRADIER_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET. Do not pass TRADIER_IS_PAPER; BotSpot derives it from paperOrLive. Example credentialValues: {"TRADIER_ACCOUNT_NUMBER":"6AB12345","TRADIER_ACCESS_TOKEN":"token..."}. Charles Schwab (schwab): SCHWAB_ACCOUNT_NUMBER + SCHWAB_TOKEN. Example credentialValues: {"SCHWAB_ACCOUNT_NUMBER":"123456789","SCHWAB_TOKEN":"base64url-token-payload..."}. Tradovate (tradovate): TRADOVATE_USERNAME + TRADOVATE_DEDICATED_PASSWORD + TRADOVATE_CID + TRADOVATE_SECRET. Optional: TRADOVATE_APP_ID, TRADOVATE_APP_VERSION. Do not pass TRADOVATE_IS_PAPER; BotSpot derives it from paperOrLive. Example credentialValues: {"TRADOVATE_USERNAME":"username...","TRADOVATE_DEDICATED_PASSWORD":"dedicated-password...","TRADOVATE_CID":"client-id...","TRADOVATE_SECRET":"secret..."}. TopstepX (projectx-topstepx): PROJECTX_TOPSTEPX_API_KEY + PROJECTX_TOPSTEPX_USERNAME. Optional: PROJECTX_TOPSTEPX_PREFERRED_ACCOUNT_NAME. Example credentialValues: {"PROJECTX_TOPSTEPX_API_KEY":"key...","PROJECTX_TOPSTEPX_USERNAME":"username..."}. WEEX (weex): WEEX_API_KEY + WEEX_API_SECRET + WEEX_API_PASSPHRASE. Example credentialValues: {"WEEX_API_KEY":"key...","WEEX_API_SECRET":"secret...","WEEX_API_PASSPHRASE":"passphrase..."}. Bitunix (bitunix): BITUNIX_API_KEY + BITUNIX_API_SECRET. Optional: BITUNIX_TRADING_MODE. Example credentialValues: {"BITUNIX_API_KEY":"key...","BITUNIX_API_SECRET":"secret..."}. Kraken (kraken): KRAKEN_API_KEY + KRAKEN_API_SECRET. Example credentialValues: {"KRAKEN_API_KEY":"key...","KRAKEN_API_SECRET":"secret..."}. Coinbase (coinbase): COINBASE_API_KEY_NAME + COINBASE_PRIVATE_KEY. Optional: COINBASE_API_PASSPHRASE, COINBASE_SANDBOX. Example credentialValues: {"COINBASE_API_KEY_NAME":"organizations/.../apiKeys/...","COINBASE_PRIVATE_KEY":"-----BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY-----..."}. memoryGb may be 2, 3, or 4 when the user sets bot memory, including because the strategy needs a browser. Omit memoryGb to keep the current size. Do not send any other size, and do not send a CPU field. CPU stays as it is. Pass memoryGb only with deploymentMode scheduled. A 2, 3, or 4 GB always-on start is rejected because that larger host is not approved; tell the user that start was not placed instead of dropping the memory setting. The tool always creates a short-lived website authorization request and returns an approval URL the user must open while signed in to BotSpot. It does not execute from chat-only approval or reusable grants. No broker secrets are returned to the MCP response. For Codex, Claude, Cursor, and other clients without BotSpot native confirmation cards, return the exact authorizationUrl as a clickable Markdown link in your reply. Do not say a card or button was created unless the client actually rendered it. BotSpot clients may render structuredContent as a native confirmation, but a button name alone is not an approval link. A pending request is not execution; only the signed-in user may approve on the website. Report expiry and check get_deployment_action_status after approval.
name: start_deployment
title: Start a live deployment
